description: TRANSYT, sold by TRL Software, is a software suite containing a macroscopic traffic model, a signal optimiser and a simulation model for designing, evaluating and modelling road junctions, from single isolated junctions to large networks mixing signal-controlled and priority junctions. The product page says its signal plans feed fixed-time signals, cableless linking, SCOOT base timings and vehicle-actuated maximum timings, and that the simulation model extends it to non-cyclic signalling, including actuated control. Coverage: drive-on-the-left and drive-on-the-right networks; features for other countries include an alternative Chilean traffic model, SCATS split times, turn-on-red flows and alternative interface terminology. Format and access: Windows desktop software (Windows 10 or later), current version 17.1.0, with an online TRL Software portal; TRL runs paid training courses (a three-day online TRANSYT 17 course is listed at GBP 850). Cost: paid; licence prices were not read. Licence: proprietary. Caveats: the traffic model equations and data formats were not read. Simulation uses: signal timing optimisation and delay and queue estimates for urban road networks, including scenarios with closed or degraded junctions. Related records: Junctions 11 (model-trl-junctions-roundabout-priority-signal-capacity), also from TRL Software, models individual roundabouts and priority junctions.
